clips.text_zh: wtf Elon 又整咗啲嘢出嚟，呢單係 flying car 喎 /biz/ 全嗰係 bullish。睇完我個 CFD account 又想 all-in TSLA 喇，cost 唔 cost 唔理住先 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Elon Musk just invented flying freaking cars, bro. The whole board is saying this is bullish. Tesla shares should react to this news on Monday. I am already thinking about adding more to my position because flying cars are a huge new market. Posts like this make me want to go all in again, even though my account is still red from last week.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about Musk inventing a flying car, board calls it bullish

signal.rationale: OP frames Musk flying-car reveal as bullish catalyst, implied buy TSLA into the news

clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk has apparently rolled out flying cars, and the entire /biz/ board is going bullish on the news. While my CFD account is still firmly in the red from last week's disasters, posts like this make me seriously consider going all in on TSLA at Monday's open. Flying cars represent a massive new market, so I'm tempted to throw caution to the wind and pile into my position despite the lingering losses.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk has once again unveiled what appears to be a flying car, and the entire /biz/ board has immediately pivoted to a bullish stance. The consensus seems to be that Tesla shares will react strongly when markets reopen on Monday, given that flying vehicles represent a substantial untapped market. Having endured a thoroughly red week, I find myself contemplating whether to double down on my existing position, because posts of this nature invariably tempt me toward reckless conviction. Cost basis be damned, as they say — conviction, however unfounded, tends to override prudence whenever Musk posts anything remotely resembling innovation.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon has, once again, unveiled something that defies credulity: an actual flying car. The entirety of /biz/ has consequently declared itself unequivocally bullish. Having absorbed the announcement, I find my CFD account trembling at the prospect of an all-in TSLA position come Monday's open, notwithstanding the gaping red hole it presently occupies. That flying vehicles constitute a categorically new market is, on this evidence, beyond dispute; the question of whether such astronomical enthusiasm can be reconciled with my surviving capital is one I shall, characteristically, defer. Cost, it seems, is a quaint relic of pre-Musk investing. Whether the contraption actually achieves sustained flight is, of course, immaterial to those who shall front-run the narrative.

clips.text_en_b2: Watch your step as you enter the Bitcoin Industries Black Swan Bear-waterfall ride, which is about to begin. Investors should keep all cash, holdings, and liquidity tucked securely inside the vehicle at all times. The ride may well prove unsuitable for certain risk profiles, as sudden drops in portfolio value can cause significant discomfort. For anyone running leveraged positions, total wipeout remains a very real possibility, so tread carefully even if the thread insists this is merely another controlled dip.
clips.text_en_c1: A /biz/ poster has helpfully announced the imminent arrival of what can only be described as a Black Swan Bear-waterfall ride for Bitcoin Industries, which one anticipates a steep and protracted descent. Please ensure that all cash, investments, and speculative positions remain securely fastened throughout the duration of this particular excursion, since the ride may prove unsuitable for those with a low tolerance for volatility. Sudden drops in portfolio worth should be expected, and for anyone foolish enough to employ leverage, the outcome is likely to be a complete and irreversible wipeout. Controlled risk, as always, sounds appealing in theory.
clips.text_en_c2: Approach the markets with circumspection, for the Bitcoin Industries Black Swan Bear-Waterfall attraction is preparing to commence operations. Patrons are advised to retain all cash, positions, and speculative liquidity securely within the vehicle throughout the duration of the ride, which executives concede may prove uncomfortable for certain board-goers. Those foolish enough to employ leverage should be apprised that sudden, precipitous declines in portfolio valuation are not merely possible but, in the present configuration, near-statistically inevitable, and total ruination remains a wholly expected outcome. This constitutes, by my count, yet another instalment in the tuition-fee curriculum of a market that punishes the imprudent with metronomic regularity, irrespective of any prior vows to exercise restraint.

clips.text_zh: 個 post 叫人嚴肅推介 stocks，個 OP 想買 SpaceX。我又諗 SpaceX 同我嗰邊 rock anchor、slope stabilization 嘅勁，但 SpaceX 點買啊 lol。Starlink 衛星發射真係 engineering 嘢嚟，但冇 retail access 都係冇 🦐
clips.text_en_b1: Someone on /biz/ asked which stocks to buy, serious answers only. He said he is leaning toward SpaceX but is open to other ideas. The thread is full of replies saying SpaceX is not publicly traded, so retail cannot buy it directly. Others suggest related plays like TSLA, Rocket Lab, or ULA suppliers. Real engineering exposure without a direct listing is hard.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking for stock picks, OP leaning SpaceX
clips.text_en_b2: Someone on /biz/ put out a serious stock picks thread, and the original poster is leaning toward SpaceX, although he's open to alternative suggestions. Most replies point out that SpaceX isn't publicly traded, so retail investors can't buy shares directly. Others recommend related plays instead, such as TSLA, Rocket Lab, or various ULA suppliers, which offer some exposure to the underlying engineering. Gaining genuine access to that kind of real-world rocketry without a direct listing remains genuinely tricky for ordinary buyers.
clips.text_en_c1: A /biz/ thread solicited serious stock recommendations, with the original poster expressing a clear preference for SpaceX while remaining receptive to alternatives. The response has been overwhelmingly pragmatic, pointing out that SpaceX remains a privately held company and therefore inaccessible to retail investors seeking direct exposure. Other contributors have proposed adjacent plays, including TSLA, Rocket Lab, and various ULA suppliers, as indirect vehicles for capitalizing on the broader aerospace sector. While Starlink's satellite deployment represents genuinely impressive engineering, the absence of any retail-accessible listing renders meaningful participation effectively impossible for the average investor.
clips.text_en_c2: An earnest solicitation has surfaced on /biz/ requesting serious stock recommendations, the original poster having tentatively settled upon SpaceX as his preferred vehicle for capital deployment, while remaining amenable to persuasion. The thread has predictably devolved into a chorus of respondents pointing out that SpaceX is, regrettably for retail aspirants, a privately held enterprise and consequently inaccessible to the man in the street. Alternative vectors have been proffered in abundance, ranging from TSLA's nebulous exposure to Rocket Lab's comparatively modest orbit and various ULA-adjacent suppliers, each offering proxy participation in genuine aerospace engineering that no direct listing can provide. The epistemic irony persists.

clips.text_zh: Anthropic 講 AI R&D 270 日後 fully automated。咁我考 FE 都未完，仲點算 lol。Engineering 都係 first wave 俾 AI 取代，slope report 都要自己寫到 😂 認真諗下轉行都未定
clips.text_en_b1: Anthropic believes AI research and development will become fully automated in about 270 days. The post says you should spend every one of those 270 days doing something meaningful. Visit your parents. Read the books you always planned to read. Make every meal count. Because there is a decent chance you only get to live normally for that amount of time before AI changes everything.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on Anthropic's 270-day AI R&D automation claim

signal.rationale: Macro AI observation, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Anthropic has suggested that AI research and development could become fully automated within roughly 270 days. The post urges people to make every single one of those days count, because normal life may be about to change beyond recognition. Visit your parents while you still can. Finally crack open those books you've been meaning to read. Put real effort into every meal you cook. There's a decent chance this is the last stretch of ordinary existence before everything flips upside down.
clips.text_en_c1: According to a recent Anthropic projection, AI-driven research and development will become fully automated within approximately 270 days, a timeline that has understandably rattled the engineering community. The accompanying post urges readers to spend each of those remaining days on something genuinely meaningful, whether that means visiting aging parents, finally tackling the books accumulating on one's nightstand, or cooking proper meals rather than defaulting to instant ramen. The implicit argument is that, once AI fully absorbs the cognitive labor underpinning modern knowledge work, ordinary life as we know it may effectively cease to exist.
clips.text_en_c2: Anthropic has posited, with characteristic algorithmic sanguinity, that artificial intelligence research and development will achieve full automation within approximately 270 days, a timeline sufficiently compressed to induce existential reflection in anyone still struggling through their Fundamentals of Engineering examination. The accompanying counsel is unfailingly poignant: dedicate each of those remaining days to something irreplaceable. Telephone your parents. Conclude the novels perpetually shelved beside your bed. Render every meal deliberate, every conversation intentional, because there exists a non-trivial probability that this particular iteration of normalcy represents the final one you shall experience before the labour market is irrevocably restructured around systems that, unlike oneself, require neither sleep nor encouragement.

clips.text_zh: pol 嗰邊笑 Musk 個 flying car 係 hover car，又話係 Tesla 底四個水 jetpack。咁啲 Elon fan 真係好易俾人 meme，但 Tesla stock 反應先係重點。同香港一樣，新聞睇完就炒，無人理個 engineering 細節 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: A /pol/ thread says being a Musk fan is a humiliation ritual. The example given is people hyping Elon's flying car as something from Blade Runner, when in reality it is just a normal Tesla with four water jetpacks attached to the bottom. The poster is mocking fans who believe every Musk reveal is revolutionary. The real product rarely matches the online hype.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread mocking Musk flying-car hype as a normal Tesla with jetpacks
clips.text_en_b2: A /pol/ thread argues that being a Musk fan has essentially become a humiliation ritual, citing the recent flying car hype as a prime example. Supporters were busy hyping it as something straight out of Blade Runner, whereas in reality it's apparently just a regular Tesla with four water jetpacks bolted to the underside. The poster mocks fans who swallow every Musk reveal as revolutionary, pointing out that the actual product rarely lives up to the online fanfare.
clips.text_en_c1: A /pol/ thread has taken to characterizing Musk fandom as something resembling a humiliation ritual, citing as evidence the breathless reception of his latest flying car unveiling. Whereas online enthusiasts have been comparing the prototype to vehicles from Blade Runner, the practical reality appears to be little beyond a standard Tesla chassis fitted with four water jetpacks bolted to the undercarriage. The poster is plainly exasperated by fans who treat every Musk announcement as though it heralded a civilizational leap forward, since the actual product so rarely lives up to the considerable hype it generates.
clips.text_en_c2: A /pol/ discussion has characterised the contemporary Musk devotee as participating in a humiliation rite, with the flying car serving as paradigmatic exhibit. The faithful, we are told, breathlessly conjured imagery drawn from Blade Runner, whereas the prosaic reality proves to be an unremarkable Tesla chassis augmented by what are, upon inspection, four glorified water jetpacks affixed to its underside. The post lampoons those disposed toward treating each corporate reveal as civilisational inflection, an inclination that persists regardless of the engineering particulars, which scarcely warrant scrutiny when share price movement beckons. The pattern, observers note, mirrors broader market behaviour in jurisdictions closer to home.

clips.text_zh: 個 anon 減咗 100 lb 由 275 變 179，仍然冇 gf。同我而家有少少似，gym 嘢做完返到屋企就係得個 mon。肥仔信今日又 tag 我睇呢啲 post，自己又唔 comment，膠膠吶 🙏 Money first ok，女友之後先算
clips.text_en_b1: An anon posted on /fit/ that he lost 100 lbs, going from 275 lbs to 179 lbs over 2.5 years. He still does not have a girlfriend. His sister made her husband take him to the gym, and the husband told him losing weight would help him find a girlfriend fast.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread, anon lost 100 lbs but still no girlfriend
clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /fit/ shared that he dropped a hundred pounds over two and a half years, going from 275 down to 179, yet he still doesn't have a girlfriend. His sister eventually made her husband take him to the gym, and the brother-in-law assured him that losing weight would help him find a partner quickly. Women at work do treat him noticeably better now, although he suspects some of that might just be down to the new job.
clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous /fit/ poster has documented a fairly substantial transformation, having shed roughly 100 pounds over the course of two and a half years, descending from 275 to 179 pounds. Despite this considerable achievement, he remains conspicuously single, a detail that evidently prompted him to share his experience. His sister eventually persuaded her husband to drag him to the gym, where the brother-in-law assured him that losing weight would rapidly improve his romantic prospects. While he acknowledges receiving notably more favorable treatment from female colleagues, he suspects the change may be attributable to his new position rather than his physique.
clips.text_en_c2: An anonymous correspondent on /fit/ has documented a transformation of considerable magnitude, having shed a hundred pounds over two and a half years, descending from a starting weight of 275 lbs to a present 179. Romantic fulfilment, however, has proved conspicuously elusive. His sister, evidently despairing of his prospects, prevailed upon her husband to escort him to the gym, where the brother-in-law offered the customary assurance that corporeal improvement accelerates romantic success. Female colleagues, the anon notes, have lately treated him with markedly increased warmth, though he suspects this may simply reflect the cachet of his new position rather than any altered perception of his intrinsic suitability. The gym, it seems, addressed only one deficiency.

The original poster professes a longstanding affection for Shiki and Higurashi, both of which date back to 2006, though this year he has expanded his autumn viewing list to include Attack on Titan, a series he is revisiting with evident enthusiasm. clips.text_en_c2: With October's advent, the customary seasonal inquiry has re-emerged on /a/, soliciting recommendations for suitably macabre anime deserving of an annual rewatch. The original poster, displaying admirable curatorial instincts, has nominated the canonical 2006 offerings Shiki and Higurashi as foundational viewing, to which he has this season appended Attack on Titan, whose grim tonal palette renders it peculiarly appropriate to the month. He further confesses to anticipating the imminent release of Edgerunners 2 with scarcely containable impatience, hoping it shall arrive in time to qualify for this autumnal survey. October, as any seasoned devotee will attest, represents the sole legitimate window for revisiting horror and psychological anime, a convention this correspondent endorses without reservation.
